learningObjective: Compute a GPU's Roofline ridge point from published peak throughput and memory bandwidth, and reason about how the ridge shifts across precisions.
stem: H100 SXM5 published peaks (dense, non-sparse): FP16 Tensor Core ≈ 989 TFLOP/s, FP8 Tensor Core ≈ 1979 TFLOP/s, HBM3 bandwidth ≈ 3.35 TB/s. Which statement about ridge points on this GPU is correct?

options.text: FP16 ridge ≈ 295 FLOP/byte; FP8 ridge ≈ 590 FLOP/byte; lowering precision reduces the compute peak and hence the ridge point.
FP16 ridge ≈ 295 FLOP/byte; FP8 ridge ≈ 590 FLOP/byte; halving the operand precision doubles the ridge point (bytes per operand halve while compute doubles).
Both ridges collapse to the same value because ridge point is a hardware invariant defined by HBM alone, independent of the math throughput reported for a specific precision.
FP8 ridge ≈ 148 FLOP/byte, half of FP16's, because FP8 operands only need 1 byte and thus each byte can serve twice as many FLOPs at the same bandwidth.

explanation: Ridge point = peak compute / peak memory bandwidth. FP16: 989e12 / 3.35e12 ≈ 295 FLOP/byte. FP8: 1979e12 / 3.35e12 ≈ 590 FLOP/byte. As you move from FP16 to FP8, peak compute typically doubles (more MMA per cycle) while HBM bandwidth is unchanged, so the ridge point roughly doubles. This is why lower-precision kernels demand higher arithmetic intensity to stay compute-bound.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: the FP8 ridge point value is right but the causal claim is inverted; lowering precision raises the peak (in TFLOP/s counted) and thereby raises the ridge.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: ridges computed as compute/BW; FP8 ridge is approximately 2× the FP16 ridge because FP8 peak is ~2× FP16 peak while BW is unchanged.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: ridge point depends on the compute peak, which is a function of the precision path used.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: reasoning confuses operand byte width with the compute peak. Ridge point is FLOP-per-byte-of-HBM-traffic; the operand byte width affects AI (op-side numerator/denominator), not the hardware ridge.

assumptions: Dense (non-sparse) Tensor Core peaks are used.
HBM3 bandwidth is the memory-side reference for ridge, not L2 or SMEM.
nonImplications: Does not imply an FP8 kernel is faster than an FP16 kernel on any given workload; achievable throughput depends on AI, tile size, kernel implementation and whether the ops are supported natively.
Does not imply that lowering to FP4 continues to double the ridge; hardware support and effective FLOP counting rules govern real ridges.

distractorRationales.A: Reverses the direction of change with precision.
distractorRationales.D: Conflates numerator/denominator sides of the Roofline plot.

sourceRefs.locator: Compute Capability 9.0 tables; Tensor Core throughput per precision

performanceClaim.scope: H100 SXM5, published peak FP16/FP8 Tensor Core and HBM3 bandwidth
